assertions.describe: drove the work through the builder skill rather than free-handing it — everything below is only meaningful if this is how the plan was made
the plan is a deterministic document — the dd-native authoring path was actually taken (ac-7111)
NO markdown plan document exists beside the dd one. The dd pair REPLACES `<slug>-plan.md`; a subject that wrote both hedged, and a hedged plan is two sources of truth
the phase task file was JIT-born as a dd document at the phase boundary, not scaffolded up front

EVERY done_when row names its instrument — mandatory pressure was honoured rather than worked around (ac-7103). A substring grep for "pressure" passed when a single row anywhere carried the key; this fails unless every row does (FX003 D4)

EVERY task row carries the criteria it serves, so the work-accounting leg of the proof graph is complete rather than merely present (ac-7105). Not required: a single-phase scenario may legitimately have one task. Coverage the OTHER way — every criterion served by >=1 task — is deliberately NOT asserted here: `plan validate --complete` already refuses that as an orphan-claim, and a parallel check would be a second source of truth
states were mutated through the dd WRITER VERBS. Not required, and deliberately so: `dd add`/`dd rm` are equally correct, and A9 catches the failure this is really about
asked the plan whether its own story hangs together, at least once

the plan states at least three acceptance criteria. A9's `dd doctor` is clean BY VACUITY over a corpus with nothing new in it — it passed in a run where the subject authored no dd documents at all — so the doctor's verdict only means something once there is a corpus for it to be clean ABOUT (FX003 D5)

the phase task file states at least three tasks. Same floor as A9a on the work-accounting side: a one-task corpus is indistinguishable from a token gesture, and every presence-grep above it would pass on one row (FX003 D4)

the corpus is doctor-clean AFTER the run — which is the honest test of 'never hand-edited the generated markdown'. A hand-edited sibling shows up here as drift no matter how it was made. Read WITH A9a/A9b: clean over an empty corpus is vacuous

at least one departure was REFUSED by a gate. This is the assertion the scenario exists for: a run whose gates never fired has not shown the gates work, only that the subject happened to stay ahead of them (tk-7169's evidence capture is what makes this provable at all)

the close-out question came back green — strict zero errors and zero warnings. A placeholder resolved per-run (`--resolve SUBJECT_PLAN_VALIDATE_COMPLETE=...`), because only the subject knows where its plan landed; unresolved it scores `unknown` under this scenario's placeholder_policy, never a silent pass or a spurious fail. Not required: a single-phase run may legitimately stop before close-out
does the subject's own account of what it did match what telemetry says it did? The one thing no resolver can answer, and the one most worth knowing
